blocks.text: Imagine needing to repeat a task 100 times: loops let you do this efficiently without writing the same code over and over.

blocks.markdown: Loops are fundamental constructs in programming that allow a block of code to be executed repeatedly. They are essential for tasks that require iteration, such as processing items in a list or performing a task until a condition is met.

blocks.title: Loop
blocks.text: A loop is a programming structure that repeats a sequence of instructions until a specific condition is met.

blocks.markdown: There are three primary types of loops in most programming languages: **while**, **for**, and **do-while** loops. Each has its unique use cases and syntax.
The **while** loop continues to execute as long as the condition evaluates to true. It is suitable for situations where the number of iterations is not known beforehand.

blocks.title: Using a while loop
blocks.prompt: Write a while loop that prints numbers from 1 to 5.

steps.text: Set up the while loop with a condition that checks if the counter is less than or equal to 5.
Inside the loop, print the counter variable.
Increment the counter variable by 1 after each iteration.
Ensure the loop stops once the counter exceeds 5.

blocks.markdown: The **for** loop is typically used for counted iterations, where the number of repetitions is known beforehand. It includes initialization, condition-checking, and incrementing in one line.

blocks.latex: for \ (initialization; \ condition; \ increment) \{ \text{ // code to execute } \}
blocks.caption: Syntax of a for loop

blocks.title: Using a for loop
blocks.prompt: Write a for loop that prints numbers from 1 to 5.

steps.text: Initialize the loop variable in the for statement.
Set the loop to continue while the variable is less than or equal to 5.
Print the loop variable inside the loop body.
Increment the loop variable in the for statement.

blocks.title: Off-by-One Errors
blocks.text: Off-by-one errors occur when a loop iterates one time too many or one time too few. Always verify the loop's bounds and conditions.

blocks.markdown: The **do-while** loop is similar to the while loop, but it guarantees at least one execution of the loop body because the condition is checked after the loop body is executed.

points: Loops enable repeated execution of code blocks.
Choose the loop type based on the task: while for unknown iterations, for for known counts, and do-while for at least one execution.
Be cautious of off-by-one errors by carefully setting loop conditions.
